newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Stals bullish on CPI, wary on Bank rate cut.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Stals bullish on CPI, wary on Bank rate cut.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Thursday he believed the inflation rate was now falling and short-term interest rates would continue to decline.
But he told state radio the central bank was still reluctant to take the lead by cutting the official Bank rate.
"We think inflation peaked in April when it was at 9.9 percent," Stals said.

"I'm farily optimistic the rate of inflation will continue to decline, that it will certainly stay below 10 percent for this year and by the end of the year it will be quite well below the present level of 9.5 percent."
Commenting on the recent decline in short-term interest rates on the interbank market, he said:

"We think that is right, that is the trend we should expect for the rest of the year...The Reserve Bank is still a little bit reluctant to take any lead in bringing interest rates down. We want to make sure we consolidate the position that the inflation rate will come down."
Figures released on Wednesday showed May's year-on-year inflation rate was 9.5 percent versus April's 9.9 percent, below the consensus expectation for a rise of 9.8 percent.
Stals added that the authorities would soon be able to assess the impact of the further relaxation of exchange controls which will see individuals permitted to invest offshore from July 1.
Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced on Wednesday that individual South Africans would be allowed to invest up to 200,000 rand overseas from next month.
"We are fairly optimistic about the trends," Stals said.
